mainTopic: Witnesses for a חזקה: one pair per year, רבי עקיבא's rule of ״דבר ולא חצי דבר״, and witnesses who differ about the crop
overview: The amud finishes the משנה about proving a three-year חזקה with a different pair of witnesses for each year. If all the pairs are proven false (הזמה), they split the payment. Three brothers who each testify with the same outside person count as three valid testimonies, but as one testimony for הזמה. The גמרא says this משנה does not follow רבי עקיבא, who holds that witnesses must prove a whole ״דבר״, not half of one. The גמרא then asks what the רבנן learn from ״דבר״. It concludes that they use it to reject two pairs who each prove only one of the two hairs of maturity, since both hairs must be present at the same time. Next, רב יהודה rules that witnesses who disagree about whether wheat or barley was grown still establish a חזקה. רב נחמן challenges him, and רב יהודה answers that both witnesses cover the same years and people do not pay attention to the crop. Finally, the גמרא quotes the brothers clause of the משנה again to begin analyzing it.

steps.title: The false witnesses split the payment three ways
steps.stepSummary: The end of the משנה's case: three pairs of witnesses, each about one year, who are proven to be עדים זוממין, divide the payment among them.
steps.simpleTranslation: They divide the payment three ways among them.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of a case that began before this section. If three pairs of witnesses each testified about one year and were all proven false, the payment is split three ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No single pair proved the whole חזקה, because each covered only one year. So no single pair pays the full value of the field. Together the three pairs caused the loss, so they share the cost.

keyTerms.meaning: They divide into three parts
Among them
Witnesses proven false through הזמה, who must pay what they tried to cause

phrases.english: They divide [the payment] three ways among them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a משנה clause that began in an earlier section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three pairs of false witnesses, each covering one year, share the payment equally.

steps.title: Three brothers with one outside witness
steps.stepSummary: Three brothers each testify about a different year, each paired with the same outside person. It counts as three testimonies, but as one testimony for הזמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Three brothers, and one other person joins with each of them. These are three separate testimonies, but they are one testimony when it comes to being proven false.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a new case: three brothers each testify about one year, and the same outsider pairs with each one. For accepting the testimony it counts as three testimonies, but for הזמה it counts as one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Brothers may not testify together. Because each brother is in a different testimony, about a different year, no testimony has two relatives in it, so it is accepted. If they are proven false, the three are treated as one testimony, so the payment is shared as in Step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: Brothers, who are relatives and may not testify together
Joins together with
Testimonies
Proving witnesses false by showing they were somewhere else at the time

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the brothers are testifying together. Each brother is in a separate pair with the outsider, and each pair covers a different year. That is why the testimony is valid.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the three yearly testimonies are separate for being accepted, but linked for paying after הזמה. It also sets up the גמרא's question of whether proving only part of a matter counts at all.

phrases.english: Three brothers,
and one [other person] joins with them –
phrases.notes: Each brother testifies about a different year, and the same outside person is the second witness with each of them.

phrases.english: these are three [separate] testimonies,
but they are one testimony regarding being proven false.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new case to the משנה that builds on the split payment in Step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three brothers, each paired with one outsider, give three valid testimonies, but they count as one testimony for הזמה.

steps.title: The משנה does not follow רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by saying that our משנה does not match the view of רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Our משנה does not follow רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes a claim about the משנה: it is not in line with רבי עקיבא. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא brings a source to prove it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה accepts witnesses who each prove only one year of a three-year חזקה. The גמרא is pointing out that רבי עקיבא would not accept that. The proof comes right after.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
Our משנה
Not in line with

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Our Mishnah is not in line with Rabbi Akiva –

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the משנה to the גמרא, which places the משנה against רבי עקיבא's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's acceptance of one-year testimonies is not like רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: The ברייתא: three pairs of witnesses make a חזקה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells of a conversation between אבא חלפתא and רבי יוחנן בן נורי. One asks about three pairs of witnesses, one pair per year, and the other answers that it is a חזקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי יוסי said: When אבא חלפתא went to רבי יוחנן בן נורי to learn תורה (and some say רבי יוחנן בן נורי went to אבא חלפתא), he asked him: If someone used a field the first year in front of two witnesses, the second year in front of two, and the third year in front of two, what is the law? He answered: It is a חזקה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its proof with a ברייתא. Two sages agree that three different pairs of witnesses, one pair for each year, are enough to make a חזקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This first half of the ברייתא matches our משנה: pairs that each prove one year combine into a full חזקה. The ברייתא is unsure who visited whom, but it does not matter for the law. The key part comes next, where רבי עקיבא disagrees.

keyTerms.meaning: He used and profited from it, meaning the field
Proof of ownership by using land openly for three years

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Yosei said:
When Abba Chalafta went
to Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri
to learn Torah,
and some say:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי אֵצֶל אַבָּא חֲלַפְתָּא
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri [went] to Abba Chalafta
to learn Torah,
he said to him:

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי שֶׁאֲכָלָהּ שָׁנָה רִאשׁוֹנָה בִּפְנֵי שְׁנַיִם,
phrases.english: If someone used [the field] the first year in front of two [witnesses],
the second [year] in front of two,
the third [year] in front of two –
what is [the law]?
He said to him: This is a chazakah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the proof for the claim in Step 3.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the משנה does not follow רבי עקיבא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא (תוספתא) reported by רבי יוסי.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: a whole matter, not half a matter
steps.stepSummary: The other sage agrees, but adds that רבי עקיבא disagrees. רבי עקיבא holds that testimony must cover a whole ״דבר״, not half of one. So the משנה does not follow him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I also say so, but רבי עקיבא disagrees about this, because רבי עקיבא would say: ״A matter״, and not half a matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The second sage agrees with the ruling but reports that רבי עקיבא disagrees. This completes the proof that our משנה does not follow רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא reads the word ״דבר״ in the פסוק to mean that witnesses must establish a complete matter. A pair that proves only one year out of three proves only part of the חזקה, so רבי עקיבא would not accept it. Our משנה does accept it, so it cannot follow רבי עקיבא.

keyTerms.meaning: I also say so
Disagrees
Half a matter, meaning only part of what needs to be proven

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא holds ״דבר ולא חצי דבר״: witnesses must prove a whole matter. Our משנה lets each pair prove just one year of a חזקה, so it does not follow רבי עקיבא.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי עקיבא is not saying the witnesses are lying or unfit. He is saying their testimony only covers part of what has to be proven, so it does not count.
steps.whyThisMatters: ״דבר ולא חצי דבר״ is a basic rule about what witnesses must prove, and the גמרא keeps building on it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: אַף אֲנִי אוֹמֵר כֵּן,
phrases.english: He said to him: I also say so,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא שֶׁרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא חוֹלֵק בְּדָבָר זֶה;
phrases.english: but Rabbi Akiva disagrees about this matter;
for Rabbi Akiva would say:
"A matter" – and not half a matter.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: אַף אֲנִי אוֹמֵר כֵּן, אֶלָּא שֶׁרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא חוֹלֵק בְּדָבָר זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא begun in Step 4 with the part that proves Step 3's claim.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה is not like רבי עקיבא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי עקיבא's reading of ״דבר״ in דברים 19:15, as reported in the ברייתא.

steps.title: What do the רבנן do with 'a whole matter'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the רבנן learn from ״דבר״ ולא חצי דבר, since they accept one pair of witnesses per year.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן, what do they do with this rule of 'a matter, and not half a matter'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about the רבנן. If they accept one pair per year, what do they use the word ״דבר״ for?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא used ״דבר״ to reject testimony about only one year of a חזקה. The רבנן disagree with him, but they also read the פסוק. So the גמרא wants to know which case they exclude with it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, here the חכמים who disagree with רבי עקיבא
A 'matter'; the word in the פסוק teaching that testimony must cover a whole thing
Half a matter, meaning testimony that covers only part of what must be proven
What do they do with it? This asks how a sage uses a source

phrases.english: And the Rabbis —
this 'a matter,' and not half a matter,
what do they do with it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from רבי עקיבא's use of ״דבר״ to ask how the רבנן use the same word.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case the רבנן exclude with ״דבר״ ולא חצי דבר.

steps.title: First suggestion: one witness for each hair
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the רבנן use ״דבר״ to reject single witnesses who each saw a different hair of maturity.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it comes to exclude a case where one witness says there is one hair on her back and the other says there is one hair on her belly...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a first answer. Maybe ״דבר״ rejects testimony where each witness saw a different one of the two hairs that show a girl has become an adult.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A girl is an adult only once she has two hairs. In this case each witness saw only one hair, so neither witness proves the full sign. The suggestion is that ״דבר״ teaches that this does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say; this opens an answer that is often rejected
To exclude a certain case
Her back
Her belly or lower abdomen

phrases.english: If you say it comes to exclude
where one says she has one hair on her back
phrases.notes: This refers to the two hairs that show a girl has become an adult.

phrases.english: and one says she has one hair on her belly;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a possible answer to the question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״דבר״ excludes two single witnesses, each about a different hair.

steps.title: That case fails anyway: it is also half a testimony
steps.stepSummary: The suggestion is rejected because each hair has only one witness, so the testimony is invalid even without ״דבר״.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this is half a matter and also half a testimony!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the first answer. That testimony is already invalid for a simpler reason, so there is no need for a פסוק to exclude it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each hair was seen by only one witness, and one witness is not enough. The testimony fails because of the number of witnesses, not because it covers half a matter. So ״דבר״ must be teaching something else.

keyTerms.meaning: Half a testimony: only one witness where two are needed

phrases.english: But this is half a matter
and half a testimony!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי חֲצִי דָבָר וַחֲצִי עֵדוּת הִיא
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proposed use of ״דבר״ in the case of single witnesses.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That case is already invalid because each hair has only one witness, so the פסוק would teach nothing new.

steps.title: Second answer: a full pair for each hair
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן use ״דבר״ to reject two full pairs, each pair testifying about only one of the two hairs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it comes to exclude a case where two witnesses say there is one hair on her back, and two say there is one hair on her belly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the answer it accepts. Even full pairs of witnesses do not count if each pair proves only one hair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here each pair is a complete testimony, but about only half of the sign, since both hairs must be there together. That is true חצי דבר. The years of a חזקה are different, because they never happen at the same time, so the רבנן accept a separate pair for each year.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; it brings a new answer after one was rejected
Two witnesses say, meaning a full valid pair

steps.whatToRemember: For the רבנן, ״דבר״ ולא חצי דבר rejects full pairs who each prove only half of one sign that must be there all at once, like the two hairs. It does not reject one pair per year of a חזקה.

phrases.english: Rather, it comes to exclude
where two say she has one hair on her back,
and two say she has one hair on her belly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer with a new one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״דבר״ excludes two pairs who each testify about only one of the two hairs.

steps.title: רב יהודה: wheat or barley, it is still a חזקה
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that if one witness says the man ate wheat from the field and the other says barley, the חזקה stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: If one witness says he ate wheat from the field and the other says he ate barley from it, this is a חזקה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from רב יהודה. Two witnesses disagree about which crop was grown, but they still establish the חזקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both witnesses agree that the man used the field during the same years. They only disagree about the crop. רב יהודה holds that this detail does not break the testimony.

keyTerms.meaning: He ate it, meaning he used and profited from the field
Presumed ownership built up through three years of use

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
If one says he ate wheat from it,
and one says he ate barley from it —
this is a חזקה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a related topic about witnesses whose testimony differs in a detail.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Witnesses who differ only about the crop still establish a חזקה.

steps.title: רב נחמן: then split years should also work
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן asks whether witnesses who each cover different years would also make a חזקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן challenged it: If so, when one witness says he used the field in years one, three and five, and the other says years two, four and six, would that also be a חזקה?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן attacks רב יהודה's ruling with a comparison. If different crops are fine, why not different years?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases each witness describes something the other did not mention. רב נחמן assumes everyone agrees the split-year case is not a חזקה. So he argues that the wheat-and-barley case should fail too.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged it
But if so; this pushes the other side's logic to a result that seems wrong
So too? This asks whether he really holds that

phrases.english: Rav Nachman challenged it:
But if so,

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד אוֹמֵר: אֲכָלָהּ רִאשׁוֹנָה שְׁלִישִׁית וַחֲמִישִׁית,
phrases.english: if one says: he used it in the first, third and fifth years,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶחָד אוֹמֵר: אֲכָלָהּ שְׁנִיָּה רְבִיעִית וְשִׁשִּׁית,
phrases.english: and one says: he used it in the second, fourth and sixth years,
would that also be a חזקה?!

steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's ruling that wheat and barley testimony makes a חזקה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If witnesses may differ about the crop, they should also be allowed to differ about the years, but that would clearly not be a חזקה.

steps.title: רב יהודה: same years versus different years
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה answers that in the split-year case each year has only one witness, but in his case both witnesses cover the same years, and people do not pay attention to the crop.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said to him: How can you compare them?! There, the year one witness testifies about, the other does not testify about. Here, both testify about the same year. What can you say, that they differ between wheat and barley? People do not pay attention to that.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה defends his ruling. He shows that the two cases are not the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב נחמן's case every year has only one witness, so no year is properly proven. In רב יהודה's case both witnesses agree on every year of use. The crop is a minor detail that people do not notice carefully, so the disagreement does not cancel the testimony.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? This rejects a comparison
Master, used here for each witness
Both of them
People do not pay attention to it

steps.whatToRemember: Two witnesses must cover the same years to make a חזקה. A small detail they would not notice, like which grain was grown, does not ruin their testimony.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יְהוּדָה: הָכִי הַשְׁתָּא?!
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said to him: How can you compare?!
There, in the year that one Master testifies about —
the other Master does not testify;

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא, תַּרְוַיְיהוּ בַּחֲדָא שַׁתָּא קָא מַסְהֲדִי.
phrases.english: here, both of them testify about the same year.
What is there to say —
that they differ between wheat and barley?
People do not pay attention to that.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יְהוּדָה: הָכִי הַשְׁתָּא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any difference between the witnesses, whether about the crop or the years, breaks the testimony.
steps.terutzMaskana: When the witnesses split the years, no year has two witnesses. A difference about the crop is a minor detail, while both still testify about the same years.

steps.title: Three brothers with one outside witness
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: three brothers, each joined by the same outside witness, give three valid testimonies for the three years of a חזקה. For הזמה, however, they are treated as one testimony.
steps.simpleTranslation: Three brothers, and one other person joins with each of them. These are three testimonies, but they count as one testimony for הזמה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now quotes again the משנה line already seen in Step 2, about three brothers and one outside witness. It is setting up the next discussion, which will analyze this ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Brothers are relatives, so they cannot testify together as a pair. So each brother testifies about a different year, and the same outside witness pairs with each one. That gives every year a valid pair of two witnesses, so the חזקה stands. But when it comes to הזמה, all three testimonies are treated as one unit.

keyTerms.meaning: Brothers. As relatives, they cannot serve as a pair of witnesses together.
Joins with. Here it means the outsider teams up with each brother to make a valid pair.
Testimonies. Each one is a separate pair of witnesses about a separate year.
Refuting witnesses by proving they were somewhere else at the time, which makes them עדים זוממין.

steps.confusionAlert: The same outside witness appears in all three testimonies, but that is not a problem. Each year still has two kosher witnesses: one brother plus the outsider. The brothers never testify together on the same year.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that one person can join different partners to form separate valid testimonies. It also raises the question of how הזמה works when testimonies are linked, and that is what the גמרא discusses next.

phrases.english: Three brothers,
and one other person joins with them,
these are three testimonies,
but they are one testimony for הזמה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רב יהודה's discussion of witnesses who differ about the crop back to the משנה's clause about three brothers (first given in Step 2), quoting it so the גמרא can analyze it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three brothers, each paired with the same outside witness for a different year, form three valid testimonies that establish a חזקה. For הזמה, they are treated as a single testimony.
